description: Machine-readable dictionary for every key in network_results.json. Units, formula and caveats for each. Generated documentation lives in docs/metrics.md; regenerate it with scripts/build_metrics_doc.py. tests/test_metrics_dictionary.py fails if a detector emits a key that is missing here.

synchrony.note: Per-bin co-activity: how many units fired at least once in the bin, over the number of units active anywhere in the recording. Saturates at one spike per unit per bin, so firing harder cannot raise it. This is the detection signal, and it is the field's convention (QSpike >=30% of active electrodes, Bakkum 2013 >=25%, Kaufman & Ziv 40%, Axion 50%, le Feber 60%). Held in plot_data under the historical name participation_fraction_signal.

population_rate_per_unit.note: Mean firing rate per active unit. Matches MaxWell's mxw.networkActivity.computeNetworkAct. Source of burst_area and peak_population_firing_rate_hz. Held in plot_data under the historical name population_firing_rate_hz.

population_rate_total.note: Unsmoothed array-wide spike rate. Rises with unit yield, so it is not comparable across wells. Source of peak_population_firing_rate_total_hz only.

mean_firing_rate_hz.definition: Firing rate of one unit over the whole recording.
mean_firing_rate_hz.caveat: Before schema 2 the denominator was the span between the first and last spike, which inflated the rate in a well quiet at either end.

cv_isi.definition: Global irregularity of a unit's inter-spike intervals.
cv_isi.caveat: Confounded by rate non-stationarity: a unit that speeds up across the recording scores high without being irregular. Prefer cv2 or lv.

cv2.definition: Local irregularity from adjacent interval pairs. 1.0 for a Poisson process.

lv.literature: Shinomoto et al. 2009 PLoS Comput Biol 5:e1000433

bimodality_coefficient.definition: Sarle's bimodality coefficient of the log-ISI distribution. Above 0.555 suggests two interval populations, i.e. intra-burst and inter-burst.
bimodality_coefficient.literature: Sarle 1990 (SAS); cutoff 0.555 is the SAS convention

is_bursty.formula: bimodality_coefficient > 0.555 AND (lv is null OR lv > 1.0)
is_bursty.definition: Whether a unit's own interval statistics look bursty.
is_bursty.caveat: Load-bearing and unvalidated: bursty units' pooled log-ISIs set reference_isi_s, which sets bin_size_ms and both merge gaps. A statistical criterion, distinct from any count of detected bursts.

start_time_s.formula: bin edge where the synchrony signal last rose above max(detection_threshold, extent_frac * peak)

end_time_s.formula: bin edge where the synchrony signal fell below the same level

burst_duration_s.definition: Burst width. At merged tiers this spans the gaps between components.
burst_duration_s.literature: Mossink et al. 2021 Stem Cell Reports (NBD)
burst_duration_s.caveat: Edges sit at a fraction of each burst's own peak, so this is not time above an absolute synchrony level. Conventions differ: QSpike uses 80% of max, Kaufman & Ziv 10% of threshold, this detector 30% of peak.

peak_time_s.formula: bin centre of the synchrony peak; at merged tiers, the peak of the highest component

peak_synchrony.definition: Largest fraction of units co-active within one bin, from the smoothed trace. Simultaneity, not breadth.
peak_synchrony.caveat: Bin-resolution simultaneity (20-100 ms), not millisecond. Smoothed, so it is a local average rather than a literal count; peak_bin_synchrony is the raw number.

peak_participation_fraction.definition: Historical name for peak_synchrony, kept so existing notebooks and collected tables keep working.
peak_participation_fraction.caveat: Misnamed. It is per-bin synchrony, NOT the maximum of participation_fraction, which measures something different.

peak_bin_synchrony.definition: Highest single-bin co-activity, from the raw unsmoothed counts.
peak_bin_synchrony.caveat: Before schema 3 this existed only on fragments and was dropped when they were merged, so network burst and superburst summaries had no un-smoothed synchrony measure.

participation_fraction.formula: units firing at least once in [start_time_s, end_time_s) / n_units, recounted from raw spike times
participation_fraction.definition: Breadth of recruitment over the whole burst. This is what the literature means by participation.
participation_fraction.literature: Bakkum et al. 2013 Nat Commun (>=25% of electrodes); QSpike Tools (>=30%)
participation_fraction.caveat: Not derived from the binned signal. Contrast with peak_bin_synchrony: a 2 s burst can reach 0.9 participation while never exceeding 0.15 in any single bin, which is sequential recruitment rather than synchrony.

burst_area.definition: Integral of the per-unit population rate across the burst.
burst_area.caveat: Yield-normalised, so comparable across wells. Nearly independent of the smoothing sigma, because Gaussian convolution preserves the integral. Before schema 3 the merged tiers summed component areas, which skipped the gaps that burst_duration_s spans.

spike_count.definition: Spikes inside the burst, summed over all units.
spike_count.literature: Mossink et al. 2021 (spikes per network burst)
spike_count.caveat: NOT divided by n_units, so it rises with unit yield. Use spikes_per_burst_per_unit to compare wells. Before schema 3 merged tiers summed components, excluding the inter-component gaps.

burst_density_hz.definition: Firing rate inside the burst, per unit that took part. Free of both duration and yield.
burst_density_hz.caveat: Computed since schema 1 to gate detection via min_burst_density_Hz, but discarded before being reported.

peak_population_firing_rate_hz.definition: Peak firing rate per active unit during the burst.
peak_population_firing_rate_hz.caveat: MEANING CHANGED IN SCHEMA 3. Before, the adaptive detector put the array-wide sum here while the Gaussian detector put the per-unit rate, so the same key differed between detectors by a factor of n_units and any table pooling both was meaningless. The array-wide value now lives in peak_population_firing_rate_total_hz.

peak_population_firing_rate_total_hz.formula: max(population_rate_total over the burst); in the Gaussian detector, peak_population_firing_rate_hz * n_units
peak_population_firing_rate_total_hz.definition: Peak array-wide spike rate during the burst.
peak_population_firing_rate_total_hz.caveat: Rises with unit yield. Do not compare across wells without n_units as a covariate.

n_components.formula: number of events merged at this tier
n_components.definition: Immediate children: fragments for a network burst, network bursts for a superburst.

n_fragments.formula: transitive sum of component fragment counts
n_fragments.definition: Burst fragments contained, at any depth. Equals n_components at the network burst tier; at the superburst tier it counts fragments while n_components counts network bursts.
n_fragments.caveat: Called component_count before schema 3, a name that read as n_components.

burst_count.definition: Number of events in this tier. Always a real number, so it distinguishes a well with no bursts from one with undefined metrics.

burst_rate_hz.caveat: Before schema 2 the denominator was the spike span, inflating the rate in wells quiet at either end.

burst_duration_p95_s.definition: Upper tail of burst duration. A culture shifting from many short bursts to a few long ones can leave the mean unchanged.

ibi_s.definition: Inter-burst interval, ONSET TO ONSET: the burst cycle period, which includes the burst itself. Network burst tier.
ibi_s.literature: Wagenaar et al. 2006 BMC Neurosci; Chiappalone et al. 2005
ibi_s.requires: at least 2 events, else all fields null

ifbi_s.definition: As ibi_s, for the burst fragment tier.

isbi_s.definition: As ibi_s, for the superburst tier.

ibi_gap_s.definition: Inter-burst interval, OFFSET TO ONSET: the silent gap. Diverges from ibi_s when bursts are long.
ibi_gap_s.caveat: Clipped at 0 so nested or overlapping tiers cannot contribute negative silences.

ifbi_gap_s.definition: As ibi_gap_s, for the burst fragment tier.

isbi_gap_s.definition: As ibi_gap_s, for the superburst tier.

spike_count_per_burst.definition: stats of the per-event spike_count. Renamed on aggregation only.

schema_version.definition: Version of this metric schema. See burst_common.SCHEMA_VERSION for what each version changed. Absent means a file written before versioning, i.e. schema 1 or 2.

detector.definition: Which detector produced the result: parameter_free or gaussian.
detector.caveat: Must be checked before pooling wells: the two detectors do not populate the same tiers, and before schema 3 they disagreed on the units of peak_population_firing_rate_hz.

analysis_window_s.definition: Span between the first and last spike. Sets the binning window; detection thresholds are estimated over this period.

duration_source.definition: "recording" if the true duration reached the detector, "spike_span" if it fell back to the active span and every rate is therefore inflated.

burst_detection_valid.definition: False means the numbers in this file are not meaningful. Filter on this first.

n_units.definition: Units with at least one spike anywhere in the recording, after curation. Denominator of the synchrony signal and of every per-unit metric.
n_units.caveat: Not a passive covariate: it sets min_units_for_burst and the threshold percentile. Plot it by group before interpreting any burst metric.

bin_size_ms.definition: Bin width for every population signal; defines what "simultaneous" means.
bin_size_ms.caveat: Adapts per well. Two wells with different bin sizes were measured with different definitions of synchrony.

reference_isi_s.definition: Biological interval scale driving bin size and the fragment merge gap.

reference_isi_source.definition: bursty_peak, all_percentile15 or default, in descending order of evidence.

participation_baseline.definition: Baseline co-activity the threshold is built from.
participation_baseline.caveat: Also echoed into plot_data for the baseline line on the trace. The Gaussian detector reports the mean rather than the median there.

participation_mad.definition: Robust spread of the synchrony signal.

participation_bc.definition: Sarle bimodality coefficient of the synchrony signal. Selects the threshold method; not a hard gate, because sparse bursting gives low BC even when real.

detection_threshold.formula: max(0.03, baseline + 0.75*MAD) if participation_bc > 0.555 else max(0.03, percentile(signal, 95 + 5*exp(-n_units/50)))
detection_threshold.definition: Synchrony level a peak had to exceed.
detection_threshold.literature: adaptive thresholding per Valkki et al. 2017 Front Comput Neurosci 11:40
detection_threshold.caveat: Adapts per well. Audit it against experimental group before reporting any phenotype. Also echoed into plot_data as the horizontal line drawn on the trace; the Gaussian detector puts null there because its threshold is in Hz, not synchrony-fraction space (see detection_threshold_hz).

threshold_source.definition: baseline_mad, or pNN.N naming the percentile used instead.

min_peak_synchrony_adaptive.definition: Raw single-bin co-activity a fragment had to reach to be kept.

min_units_for_burst.definition: Absolute co-active unit floor behind min_peak_synchrony_adaptive.

fragment_merge_gap_s.formula: percentile(intra-burst ISIs of bursty units, 95), else 3 * reference_isi_s
fragment_merge_gap_s.definition: Largest gap across which two fragments may join into one network burst.

nb_merge_gap_s.formula: antimode of log10(inter-fragment intervals), else max(network_merge_gap_min, 0.3)
nb_merge_gap_s.definition: Largest gap across which network bursts may join into a superburst.
nb_merge_gap_s.literature: 0.3 s floor from Tsodyks & Markram 1997 PNAS (vesicle recovery)

superburst_merge_gap_s.definition: Duplicate of nb_merge_gap_s, kept for call-site compatibility.

superburst_min_components.definition: Minimum network bursts in a superburst, default 2.
superburst_min_components.literature: Wagenaar et al. 2006 define a superburst as a cluster
superburst_min_components.caveat: Was effectively 1 before schema 2, so every network burst longer than superburst_min_dur_s was also reported as a superburst. Superburst counts from schema 1 files are not comparable.

sigma_participation_bins.definition: Gaussian smoothing width applied to the synchrony signal, 1-2 bins.

sigma_firing_rate_bins.definition: Gaussian smoothing width applied to the per-unit rate, 3-8 bins. Wider because the rate is an unbounded count while synchrony is bounded and pre-averaged.
sigma_firing_rate_bins.caveat: Affects the drawn trace and little else: burst_area is an integral, which Gaussian convolution preserves.

method.definition: gaussian_population_rate_mean_plus_sd, or ..._no_height_gate when min_height_sd is disabled.

gaussian_sigma_s.definition: Smoothing kernel sigma, default 0.1 s. Mirrors MATLAB GaussianSigma.

baseline_mean_hz.formula: mean(smoothed rate over the whole trace)
baseline_mean_hz.caveat: Taken over the whole trace including bursts, so it rises with burst load. The literature convention, deliberately kept, but not a pure baseline.

baseline_std_hz.definition: Standard deviation behind the height gate; same whole-trace caveat as baseline_mean_hz.

min_height_sd.definition: Height gate in units of baseline_std_hz, default 2.0. None disables it.
min_height_sd.literature: Chiappalone et al. 2005 use mean + N*SD
min_height_sd.caveat: Added in schema 2. Without it a silent well still yielded network bursts.

detection_threshold_hz.definition: Rate a peak had to exceed.

min_prominence_hz.definition: Peak prominence requirement; defaults to baseline_std_hz.

onset_offset_peak_frac.definition: Burst edges sit where the smoothed rate falls to this fraction of the peak.
onset_offset_peak_frac.caveat: Before schema 2 the code used peak * (1 - frac) instead of peak * frac, making durations roughly three times too short.

edge_rule.definition: fraction_of_peak. Records which edge convention produced the durations.

time_s.definition: Bin centres for every trace in plot_data.

participation_fraction_signal.caveat: Misnamed: per-bin synchrony, not the per-burst participation_fraction. plot_data keys are splatted into helper.plot_clean_network as keyword arguments, so they cannot be renamed or extended without changing that signature.

population_firing_rate_hz.definition: The smoothed per-unit rate trace. Historical name.
population_firing_rate_hz.caveat: Misnamed: this is per unit, not an array-wide sum, and so differs from the event field peak_population_firing_rate_total_hz.

nb_peak_participation_fraction.definition: peak_synchrony of every network burst. Historical name.

sb_start_times_s.definition: Superburst onsets; empty for the Gaussian detector.

sb_end_times_s.definition: Superburst offsets; empty for the Gaussian detector.

stats_fields.description: Tier metrics derived from a per-event field are reported as an object rather than a scalar.
stats_fields.mean: arithmetic mean, or null when no event defined the field
stats_fields.cv: std/mean, or null when the mean is within 1e-12 of zero
stats_fields.null_convention: A well with no bursts has an undefined mean, reported as null rather than 0.0. Before schema 2 these were zeros, which dragged group means down and made a silent well look like one with very short bursts. burst_count is always a real number, so the two cases are distinguishable.
